title: Tomorrow
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, small snowbound American river town in deep winter, a vintage walnut shortwave radio with a warm amber dial glowing against cold blue night, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 1. Her grandfather's radio reads tomorrow's news. 📻

Original fiction. Part 2 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Lena Shaw's grandfather left her three things. A pocket watch. A stack of unpaid bills. And a radio he made her promise never to sell.
scenes.image: an antique walnut shortwave radio on a kitchen table beside a frosted window at night, snow falling outside

scenes.narration: It was a shortwave set, older than her mother. Brass knobs. Cloth speaker. A dial that glowed the color of whiskey.
scenes.image: extreme close-up of a glowing amber radio dial and brass knobs in a dark room

scenes.narration: The first night, it only hissed. Then, at two minutes to midnight, a man's voice cut through the static. Calm. Clear. Good evening, Millbrook. Here is tomorrow's news.
scenes.image: young woman in a dark kitchen leaning toward an old radio, her face lit amber by the dial

scenes.narration: He read the weather. Snow by sunrise. Then an accident. A blue pickup truck. The Route Nine bridge. Seven forty in the morning.
scenes.image: an empty iron bridge over a frozen river at night under a single streetlight

scenes.narration: Lena laughed. A pirate station. An old recording. Something Grandpa taped years ago and left on a loop.
scenes.image: woman lying awake in bed, the faint amber glow of a radio spilling through the bedroom doorway

scenes.narration: At seven, she opened the curtains. It was snowing. The forecast had said clear skies all week.
scenes.image: heavy snow falling past a bedroom window at grey dawn, a woman's hand holding the curtain

scenes.narration: She drove to the bridge and parked on the shoulder with the engine running. Seven thirty-eight. Seven thirty-nine.
scenes.image: woman gripping the steering wheel of a parked car on a snowy roadside, wipers frozen mid-sweep

scenes.narration: A blue pickup came around the bend, too fast. It fishtailed. It hit the railing.
scenes.image: a blue pickup truck skidding sideways on a snowy bridge, headlights cutting through falling snow

scenes.narration: It hung there, nose down over the frozen river. The driver climbed out, shaking, unhurt. Exactly like the voice said.
scenes.image: a blue pickup truck tipped through a bent bridge railing over a frozen river, a man standing safely beside it

scenes.narration: That night, at two minutes to midnight, the radio cleared its throat. Good evening, Millbrook. Tomorrow, there will be a fire.
scenes.image: close-up of the old radio's speaker grille glowing in a pitch-dark kitchen, snow-light on the window
